tasks.title: Run the readiness gate over a ticket document prepare did not author
tasks.objective: Let an operator put an existing committed ticket document through the adversarial readiness gate, so a hand-written graph gets the same intake scrutiny as a generated one instead of none.
acceptance_criteria: The gate logic in `preparation.py` is reachable for a committed ticket document that no preparation turn produced, without `prepare` running a planning turn first, and `prepare` keeps its current behavior unchanged.

The command reads the ticket document and the repository only. It writes no ticket document, starts no run, and touches neither the ledger nor Git, so a graph cannot be silently rewritten by being inspected.

The adapter rule is restated for this case and enforced: `prepare` refuses a gate on the adapter that authored the graph, and a hand-written graph has no authoring adapter, so the rule becomes an explicit operator choice with a recorded default rather than an inherited `_GATE_DEFAULT` lookup.

Provenance records the gate adapter, model, and the SHA-256 of the exact ticket document bytes that were gated, so a later edit is traceably a different input, which is the role `provenance.source_sha256` plays for a prepared graph.

Questions are reported and the exit code distinguishes a clean gate from one with open questions; neither outcome edits the document, and reporting is the default with any blocking behavior explicitly requested.
Tests cover a clean document, a document with open questions, refusal of the authoring adapter, and a document whose bytes changed between two gate runs, using a fake adapter and never a live model.
